daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

President Prabowo defended the government against accusations of lying about food self-sufficiency, calling such claims "sinful" and saying many smart people are accusing the government of dishonesty. He separately reported receiving data showing double-digit percentage increases in vehicle purchases by farmers. The president also commented on fuel subsidies, stating that Lamborghini owners should pay expensive fuel prices.

  • The DPR called for anyone involved in the burning of three santri in Lombok to be firmly prosecuted regardless of position.
  • Commission III of the DPR urged TNI, Polri, and the Attorney General's Office to remain unified and solid.
  • The Home Affairs Minister instructed regional heads not to furlough PPPK (government contract employees).
  • The Communications and Digital Affairs Ministry proposed that the One Data policy should not open access to personal data.
  • The Home Affairs Minister requested that Indonesia's One Data system be strengthened to prevent hacking.
  • The Coalition of Civil Society for Free Elections (Kospi) announced that a judicial review decision on the State Budget Law regarding free meal programme funds will be read in July.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia urged the United States and Iran to de-escalate amid heavy military strikes between the two countries, with the Foreign Ministry calling on all parties to pursue de-escalation. Indonesia sent a high-level delegation to honor Iran's late Supreme Leader. Former President Megawati received Timor-Leste's highest state honor and delivered a presidential lecture emphasizing reconciliation between the two nations.

  • The National Resilience Institute (Lemhannas) said the BrahMos missile deal will boost Indonesia's defense industry.
  • Indonesia is closely monitoring developments regarding China's ballistic missile tests.
  • The Foreign Ministry is assisting with the repatriation of remains of an Indonesian citizen who drowned in a lake in Germany.
  • Saudi Arabia appreciated Indonesia's synergy in successfully implementing the 2026 hajj pilgrimage.
  • The Trade Minister announced plans to expand coconut and CPO exports to Lebanon.

Other

President Prabowo officially launched the B50 biodiesel program to boost energy sovereignty, making Indonesia the first country to implement a 50 percent biodiesel blend. The mandatory B50 rollout is expected to end diesel imports entirely, with Prabowo emphasizing that farmers should benefit most from the program. Energy Minister Bahlil stated the B50 biodiesel is safe for Asian and European cars.

  • Indonesia launched a carbon registry to accelerate carbon trading, with the Financial Services Authority and Forestry Minister emphasizing benefits for grassroots communities.
  • The government plans to turn diesel surplus into jet fuel to end imports of aviation fuel.
  • Indonesia will build methanol industries to support the B50 biodiesel program.
  • The Communications Ministry is planning new spectrum allocation for future 6G networks.
  • Indonesia and Russia agreed to deepen intellectual property partnership to boost innovation.
